data.name: TNKS2 (Tankyrase-2)
data.description: Tankyrase-2, a PARP family enzyme; its loss activates AMPK and suppresses mTORC1, impairing adipocyte differentiation.
data.description_beginner: An enzyme related to the PARP family. Removing it switches on the AMPK brake and dials down mTORC1, which in cultured fat-cell precursors stops them from maturing properly. This was shown in a cell line, not yet in an animal.

studies.title: Tankyrase-2 regulates adipocyte differentiation through AMPK/mTOR signaling.
studies.authors: Rauch B; Ujlaki G; Poliska S; Murahwa N; Kovacs P; Pettko-Szandtner A; Uray K; Bai P

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Deleting TNKS1 or TNKS2 slows adipocyte differentiation, with inhibited autophagy, AMPK activation and suppressed mTORC1; the TNKS2-knockout defect is rescued by NV-5138 or by LKB1 inhibition, and TNKS2 ADP-ribosylates LKB1 (cell line).
